thread.title: California men's rowing begins new season at California Cup Challenge

author: golden state today
title: California men's rowing begins new season at California Cup Challenge
text:
The California men’s rowing team is set to begin its 2026 season at the California Cup Challenge, which will take place this Saturday in Newport Beach. Hosted by UC Irvine, the event will feature two young Golden Bear crews: the freshmen eight and the fourth varsity eight. They are scheduled to compete against several top teams from Southern California.
The competition will follow a format of rotating dual races over roughly 1,400 meters. Cal’s fourth varsity eight (4V8+) opens against UC Santa Barbara at 8:10 a.m., followed by the freshmen eight racing host UC Irvine at 8:15 a.m. In round two, Cal’s 4V8+ faces Orange Coast College at 9:45 a.m., with the freshmen eight meeting UCLA right after at 9:50 a.m. Winners from each matchup will advance to Round 3, where they can compete for six trophies awarded around 12:15 p.m.
This regatta marks Cal’s first chance this year to test itself against outside opponents following months of training since the academic year began. Head coach Scott Frandsen has put together a roster featuring both returning athletes and new talent vying for spots on key boats.
“I’m pleased with how the squad has pushed through the training over the past 6-7 months,” Frandsen said. “We’ve been working to establish our depth through the entire team and to really embed the framework of how we row. The focus, enthusiasm and persistence has been outstanding. We are now in the phase of the year where we are starting to test out different lineups and see if we can find crews that can really click.”
Cal aims to build on last year’s third-place finish in the James Ten Eyck standings at nationals as it looks ahead toward another appearance at the IRA Championship later this season. The Bears bring back five rowers from last season’s first varsity eight—Tobias Kristensen, Tim Roth, Gennaro di Mauro, Noah Anger, and Pablo Moreno.
Several members of this year’s squad gained international experience over summer by competing in Poznan, Poland at the World U23 Championships; five earned medals there for their respective countries.
Moreno took silver for Spain in men’s four while Matthew Waddell earned silver with New Zealand’s men’s eight; Anger, Johannes Benien and Maximilian Pfautsch helped Germany secure bronze in their event. Other Bears representing their nations included Jeremy Beale (Australia), Xavier Gagnon (United States), Osian James (Great Britain) and Nat Gauden (Great Britain).
“There is always a bit of impatience in this part of the year as the guys all want to get to the heart of our racing schedule,” Frandsen said. “We need to bring that same intensity and focus to each day of training and each step towards those big races. We can’t get ahead of ourselves and look too many steps down the path.”
Spectators planning to attend are encouraged to gather near Marina Park Community Center lighthouse for optimal viewing and audio during races. Those unable to be present have options for following along via live stream or checking live results online.
For updates throughout Cal men’s rowing season, fans can follow @CalMrowing on Twitter or Instagram or visit Cal Crew on Facebook.
